Hi Evelyn,

We started seeing intermittent 502s and a big jump in websocket latencies in our integration this morning (around 09:00 PDT). The behavior shows up when a few simultaneous sessions start streaming long transcripts — the client sees partial frames and then a 502. We've attached a short log sample and a graph of requests/502s.

Symptoms:
- 502 Bad Gateway spikes to ~8% of streaming requests between 09:00-09:12
- Median end-to-end latency jumped from ~120ms to ~650ms
- When it happens, streams sometimes deliver the first chunk(s) then close with a 502

This is impacting our demo environment and a handful of production users. Can you confirm whether this is a client-side reconnect issue or something upstream in your stack? We need this triaged quickly — happy to allow a maintenance window if you need it.

Attachments:
- 500-log-sample.txt (snippet, references request ids)
- caduceus-502-spike.png

Thanks,
Alicia

TL;DR — proxy upstream timeouts cascading into chunked-transfer closes; model runtime p95 increased under burst.

Prelim findings from the first pass on traces (attached proxy-trace-20280411.har):
- A subset of requests shows the upstream model runtime hitting ~28–34s (p95), which exceeds the proxy read_timeout and triggers a connection close; clients then surface 502 Bad Gateway.
- The proxy keeps alive the socket, but chunked transfer semantics + abrupt upstream close leads to partial frames delivered then connection teardown.
- Error-rate spike correlates with a burst of long-lived sessions starting at 09:02 and again at 09:06 where session concurrency briefly doubled.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (can be enacted in <15 mins):
1) Route traffic from the affected customer to the previous model variant (known stable p95 ~16s) via runtime traffic-split.
2) Reduce proxy read_timeout from 60s -> 35s to fail faster and avoid partial-frame exposures; couple with a client-facing retry policy for resumed streaming.
3) Temporarily enable non-streaming fallback for long transcripts (batch polling) for sessions that exceed N tokens in first 10s.

I’ve attached the HAR with example request ids (proxy-trace-20280411.har). If we do route to the older variant, we should expect a drop in p95 and near-zero 502s while we continue debugging model-side tail latency.

—David
